title: An exponential upper bound on the number of bipartitions of a sparse-boundary set with few internal edges
author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the counting lemma for bipartitions of a set with a small boundary (author lemma at source lines 1344-1364, label lem:two-colour-count), together with its weighted corollary eq:colouring-weight. The proof (source lines 1366-1414) has real content: it defines an exceptional set X of vertices that are either too poorly connected inside H or too concentrated in their own class (proof lines 1372-1376), bounds its size by a degree-summing computation that turns the boundary and internal-edge hypotheses into |X| = O(|R| log d / d) (proof lines 1377-1379), and then counts the admissible bipartitions by choosing the small side inside X and the remaining vertices by their degrees, which yields exp(O(|R| log^2 d / d)) (proof lines 1380-1404). The weighted consequence is obtained by substituting that bound and using the parameter relation ln n >= (ln 2/(M-1)) d (proof lines 1405-1413). H2.
